questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to coordinate multi-region progressive rollouts using native GCP tools while handling regional performance optimizations and feature flags.

## Key Concepts
- Regional traffic management with Cloud Deploy for controlled, phased rollouts
- Cloud Run min_instances per region to reduce cold-start latency
- Cloud Monitoring for per-region latency and error alerting
- Traffic shifts as a safe rollback mechanism
- Least-privilege IAM bindings for deployment security

## Implementation Steps
```bash
# 1. Build and push v2 image to Artifact Registry
gcloud builds submit --tag \
  us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/repo/file-upload-api:v2

# 2. Create Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline with per-region targets
cat <<EOF > clouddeploy.yaml
apiVersion: deploy.cloud.google.com/v1
kind: DeliveryPipeline
metadata:
  name: file-upload-pipeline
spec:
  regions:
    - us-central1
    - europe-west1
    - asia-east1
---
apiVersion: deploy.cloud.google.com/v1
kind: Target
metadata:
  name: us-central1
spec:
  run:
    location: projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/us-central1
  ingress:
    traffic:
      - percent: 33
        toTarget: us-central1
---
apiVersion: deploy.cloud.google.com/v1
kind: Target
metadata:
  name: europe-west1
spec:
  run:
    location: projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/europe-west1
  ingress:
    traffic:
      - percent: 33
        toTarget: europe-west1
---
apiVersion: deploy.cloud.google.com/v1
kind: Target
metadata:
  name: asia-east1
spec:
  run:
    location: projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/asia-east1
  ingress:
    traffic:
      - percent: 33
        toTarget: asia-east1
EOF

# 3. Configure per-region min_instances in Cloud Run service
gcloud run deploy file-upload-api \
  --image us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/repo/file-upload-api:v2 \
  --region us-central1 \
  --min-instances 2

gcloud run deploy file-upload-api \
  --image us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/repo/file-upload-api:v2 \
  --region europe-west1 \
  --min-instances 2

gcloud run deploy file-upload-api \
  --image us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/repo/file-upload-api:v2 \
  --region asia-east1 \
  --min-instances 2

# 4. Set up Cloud Monitoring alerts for latency and errors
cat <<EOF > alerts.yaml
conditions:
  - displayName: "High Latency - File Upload API"
    conditionThreshold:
      filter: resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND
        metric.type="run.googleapis.com/container/response_latency"
      comparison: COMPARISON_GT
      thresholdValue: 5000
      duration: 300s
      aggregations:
        - alignmentPeriod: 60s
          perSeriesAligner: ALIGN_MEAN
  - displayName: "High Error Rate - File Upload API"
    conditionThreshold:
      filter: resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND
        metric.type="run.googleapis.com/container/error_count"
      comparison: COMPARISON_GT
      thresholdValue: 10
      duration: 300s
      aggregations:
        - alignmentPeriod: 60s
          perSeriesAligner: ALIGN_SUM
alertPolicies:
  - displayName: "File Upload API - High Latency"
    combiner: OR
    conditions: [ref: conditions[0]]
    notificationChannels: [NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_ID]
  - displayName: "File Upload API - High Error Rate"
    combiner: OR
    conditions: [ref: conditions[1]]
    notificationChannels: [NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL_ID]
EOF

gcloud alpha monitoring policies create --policy-from-file=alerts.yaml

# 5. Deploy v2 using Cloud Deploy
gcloud deploy releases create v2-release \
  --delivery-pipeline-file=clouddeploy.yaml \
  --images=file-upload-api=us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/repo/file-upload-api:v2

# 6. Rollback by shifting traffic to v1
gcloud deploy rollouts promote v2-release \
  --delivery-pipeline=file-upload-pipeline \
  --to-target=us-central1 --traffic=0

gcloud deploy rollouts promote v2-release \
  --delivery-pipeline=file-upload-pipeline \
  --to-target=europe-west1 --traffic=0

gcloud deploy rollouts promote v2-release \
  --delivery-pipeline=file-upload-pipeline \
  --to-target=asia-east1 --traffic=0
```

## Minimal IAM Bindings
```bash
# Allow Load Balancer to invoke Cloud Run
gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding file-upload-api \
  --member=serviceAccount:PROJECT_NUM-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/run.invoker \
  --region=all

# Allow Cloud Deploy to manage Cloud Run
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding PROJECT_ID \
  --member=serviceAccount:clouddeploy-prod@PROJECTS.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/run.admin

# Allow Cloud Build to push to Artifact Registry
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding PROJECT_ID \
  --member=serviceAccount:PROJECT_NUM@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/artifactregistry.writer
```

## Rollback Procedure
In Cloud Deploy, a rollback is executed by promoting the previous rollout or shifting traffic back to v1. This is done by updating the traffic percentage in the target configuration to route 100% of traffic back to the v1 revision.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design end-to-end progressive delivery using only Google-native tools, with real-time metrics, cross-region concerns, and safe rollback. It emphasizes the integration of CI/CD, traffic management, and observability.

## Key Concepts
- Progressive canary deployment across revisions with time-based traffic ramping
- Cross-region latency and error rate monitoring using Cloud Monitoring
- SLO-based alerting with automated rollback triggers
- Minimal IAM for deployment and operations

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Publish v2 to Artifact Registry
Build and push the container image using Cloud Build or a local Docker build:

```bash
# Option A: Using Cloud Build
gcloud builds submit --tag us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/chat-gateway/v2 .

# Option B: Local build and push
docker build -t us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/chat-gateway/v2 .
gcloud auth configure-docker us-docker.pkg.dev
docker push us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/chat-gateway/v2
```

### 2. Deploy v2 with Traffic Split
Deploy the new revision and configure progressive canary traffic splitting:

```bash
# Deploy v2 revision
SERVICE_NAME=chat-gateway
gcloud run deploy $SERVICE_NAME \
  --image us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/chat-gateway/v2 \
  --region us-central1

# Get the v2 revision name
V2_REVISION=$(gcloud run revisions list --service $SERVICE_NAME --region us-central1 --format='value(name)' | head -1)
V1_REVISION=$(gcloud run revisions list --service $SERVICE_NAME --region us-central1 --format='value(name)' | tail -1)

# Apply traffic split: 10% to v2 for 8 minutes
gcloud run traffic update $SERVICE_NAME \
  --region us-central1 \
  --to-revisions $V2_REVISION=10%,$V1_REVISION=90%

# After 8 minutes, update to 30% for 16 minutes
gcloud run traffic update $SERVICE_NAME \
  --region us-central1 \
  --to-revisions $V2_REVISION=30%,$V1_REVISION=70%

# After 24 minutes total, promote v2 to 100%
gcloud run traffic update $SERVICE_NAME \
  --region us-central1 \
  --to-revisions $V2_REVISION=100%
```

### 3. Cross-Region Health Checks and Monitoring
Configure Cloud Monitoring to track regional metrics:

**Create SLOs:**
- **p95 Latency SLO:** Target threshold 350ms over 5-minute sliding window
- **Error Rate SLO:** Target threshold 99.5% (max 0.5% errors) over 5-minute window

**Alert Policy Configuration:**
```bash
# Create alerting policy for p95 latency
cat > latency-alert.json << EOF
{
  "displayName": "Chat Gateway p95 Latency",
  "conditions": [
    {
      "displayName": "p95 latency > 350ms",
      "conditionThreshold": {
        "filter": "resource.type=\"cloud_run_revision\" AND metric.type=\"run.googleapis.com/container latency\"",
        "aggregation": {
          "alignmentPeriod": "60s",
          "perSeriesAligner": "ALIGN_PERCENTILE_95"
        },
        "comparison": "COMPARISON_GT",
        "thresholdValue": 0.35,
        "duration": "300s",
        "trigger": {
          "count": 1
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "combiner": "OR",
  "enabled": true
}
gcloud alpha monitoring policies create --policy-from-file=latency-alert.json
```

```bash
# Create alerting policy for error rate
cat > error-alert.json << EOF
{
  "displayName": "Chat Gateway Error Rate",
  "conditions": [
    {
      "displayName": "Error rate > 0.5%",
      "conditionThreshold": {
        "filter": "resource.type=\"cloud_run_revision\" AND metric.type=\"run.googleapis.com/container/request_count\"",
        "aggregation": {
          "alignmentPeriod": "60s",
          "perSeriesAligner": "ALIGN_RATE"
        },
        "comparison": "COMPARISON_GT",
        "thresholdValue": 0.005,
        "duration": "300s",
        "trigger": {
          "count": 1
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "combiner": "OR",
  "enabled": true
}
gcloud alpha monitoring policies create --policy-from-file=error-alert.json
```

### 4. Automated Rollback
When alerts trigger, shift traffic back to v1:

```bash
# Immediate rollback to v1 (100% traffic)
gcloud run traffic update $SERVICE_NAME \
  --region us-central1 \
  --to-revisions $V1_REVISION=100%
```

### 5. Minimal IAM Roles
Assign the following roles to the deployment/service account:

| Role | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `roles/run.invoker` | Allows traffic invocation to Cloud Run service |
| `roles/artifactregistry.reader` | Pull container images from Artifact Registry |
| `roles/monitoring.alertPolicyUser` | Create and manage alerting policies |

### 6. Testing Failover

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Assess ability to design multi-region, traffic-controlled deployments using native GCP tooling while implementing proper monitoring, alerting, and rollback mechanisms with minimal IAM permissions.

## Key Concepts

- Cross-region blue/green canary deployment strategy
- Per-region traffic splitting with Cloud Run
- Cloud Monitoring alert policies with regional metrics
- Artifact Registry image management and deployment
- IAM least privilege for service accounts and automation

## Code Example

```bash
# Build and push images to Artifact Registry
gcloud builds submit --tag us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/REPO/api:v2
gcloud builds submit --tag eu-west1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/REPO/api:v2

# Deploy v2 to both regions
gcloud run deploy api-v2 --image us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/REPO/api:v2 --region us-central1 --no-traffic
gcloud run deploy api-v2 --image eu-west1-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT/REPO/api:v2 --region eu-west1 --no-traffic

# Configure 20% traffic split to v2
gcloud run services update-traffic api --region us-central1 --revisions api-v2=20,api-v1=80
gcloud run services update-traffic api --region eu-west1 --revisions api-v2=20,api-v1=80
```
